security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline labels, and documentation links. The real concerns are install examples that ask users to run npx commands and fetch remote registry content. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or hidden malicious instruction was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Remote shadcn registry install in the Quick Start block.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the shadcn package version, document review steps for fetched registry content, and provide checksums or a vendored copy.

remediation.issue: Related-skills examples run npx skills add against community skill references.
remediation.suggestion: Mark these commands as optional, pin install targets to immutable refs, and tell users to inspect each skill before installation.

finding_verdicts.reason: The fenced Quick Start block contains an npx shadcn command that fetches a registry from ui.inference.sh and modifies a project. That is a real supply-chain risk if users run it without review.

content.value_statement: Agent output often needs interactive UI instead of plain text. This skill shows how to render structured widget definitions as React and Next.js components.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to add the widgets registry with shadcn.
Shows WidgetRenderer usage with Widget and WidgetAction types.
Documents layout, typography, interactive, and display widget types.
Demonstrates flight card and contact form widget structures.
Shows submit and click action handling patterns.
limitations: Requires a React or Next.js project with compatible component setup.
The Quick Start downloads remote registry content that should be reviewed.
Does not implement backend validation, storage, or authentication.
Examples are guidance, not a complete application architecture.

use_cases.title: Build Agent Forms
use_cases.description: Create interactive forms from structured responses for contact, intake, or workflow tasks.

use_cases.title: Display Rich Agent Results
use_cases.description: Render cards, badges, images, and layouts for travel, support, or product data.

use_cases.title: Prototype Generative UI
use_cases.description: Test JSON-driven interface patterns before committing to custom component design.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Basic Widget
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simple display widget.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use widgets-ui to create a simple React widget that displays a title, body text, and one action button.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Form Widget
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a structured form for user input.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use widgets-ui to design a contact form widget with name, email, message, and submit action handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Data Card
prompt_templates.scenario: Present structured data in a compact UI.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use widgets-ui to create a card for flight details with departure, arrival, status, icon, and supporting text.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Agent Actions
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced integration with generated UI and host callbacks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use widgets-ui to plan a React integration where agent-generated widgets trigger click and submit callbacks with form data.

output_examples.input: A support agent needs a contact form for collecting customer details.
output_examples.output: A form widget plan with fields for name, email, and message, plus a submit action for the host app.

output_examples.input: A travel assistant needs to show a flight summary.
output_examples.output: A compact card layout with departure, arrival, route icon, status label, and readable spacing.

output_examples.input: A product assistant needs selectable plan options.
output_examples.output: An interactive widget plan with labels, select options, confirmation text, and an action callback.

best_practices: Review remote registry content before adding it to a project.
Validate all submitted form data on the server.
Keep widget schemas small, explicit, and easy to inspect.
anti_patterns: Do not trust agent-generated form values without validation.
Do not run install commands from unreviewed sources.
Do not use widgets as a replacement for authentication or authorization.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps render structured JSON widget definitions as React and Next.js user interfaces.

faq.question: Does it include backend logic?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on frontend rendering, widget structure, and action handling patterns.

faq.question: Can it render forms?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples include inputs, textareas, checkboxes, selects, and submit actions.

faq.question: Is the install command risk free?
faq.answer: No. The command downloads remote registry content, so users should inspect it before use.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it display rich cards?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents cards, rows, columns, badges, icons, images, captions, and gradients.
